logo_override.validation_detail: webfetch returned 'Image fetched successfully', confirming HTTP 200 plus a real image content type. Declared by the site as <link rel="apple-touch-icon" href="/themes/custom/bond_theme/favicon/apple-touch-icon.png" sizes="180x180">. Decoded and rendered: the Bond University coat of arms (shield, Southern Cross, waratah and book) as white line-art on an OPAQUE dark navy #1D304E rounded-square field. Because the navy field is opaque rather than transparent, the pale artwork still reads clearly on a light card, and as a png it carries no conditional CSS that could recolour it.

notes: Bond required real digging and the obvious answer is not reportable. The header brand is an INLINE svg with no src, so there is no URL to probe: , with a second .bond-logo-outline variant toggled by CSS. Per rule 5 I will not manufacture a URL for an inline asset. Rejected og:image / link rel=image_src on both pages tried (https://bond.edu.au/scholarship/bond-university-postgraduate-research-scholarship and https://bond.edu.au/our-university): both point at campus photography, e.g. /sites/default/files/2022-07/2020_FSD_Building%20Exterior_CAV_1.jpg and /sites/default/files/2022-08/2016_Bond_Campus_Aerial_Quad.jpg - not a mark. Also rejected /themes/custom/bond_theme/favicon/icon.svg even though it probes HTTP 200 image/svg+xml and is a proper navy crest: its first line is , so a visitor whose OS is in dark mode gets a WHITE crest - invisible on a light card, which is exactly the rule 3 failure. An SVG referenced from an evaluates prefers-color-scheme against the reader's OS, not the card, so that risk is real and cannot be designed away. The apple-touch-icon.png has no such conditional styling and an opaque background, so it is the only probeable Bond asset that is unconditionally safe on a light card; it is a crest rather than a wordmark, which is the lesser compromise the brief allows. Provenance: Bond University's own coat of arms, on its own bond.edu.au domain, for a Bond University award - rule 2 satisfied. Third-party logo repositories that dominate search results for this logo (brandfetch.com, seeklogo, brands of the world, vectorseek, iconlogovector) were deliberately not used, per rule 6.
